question: When AI produces results faster than experts can check them, how do we decide what to trust?
reflection: Careful checking is slow, but it is how new knowledge becomes something everyone can safely build on.

sources.subject: Anthropic Dashboards, OpenAI Decisions API, Claude Pen Testing

one_line: AI output is outpacing human review, from a flood of unchecked maths papers to persistent agents that work for days as digital coworkers.

top_stories.title: OpenAI's maths papers outpace peer review
top_stories.what: Most of OpenAI's 700-plus AI-written maths manuscripts have not been independently reviewed, few show the model's reasoning, and one high-profile proof reportedly has a computer check that does not match its written argument.
top_stories.why: Any team using AI to draft research needs clear review steps, because a confident output and a verified result are not the same thing.

top_stories.title: Google launches Gemini agents that act like coworkers
top_stories.what: Google introduced business Gemini agents that keep working for hours or days, carry memory across apps, and can get their own email, storage, permissions and audit trail.
top_stories.why: Treating an agent as a team member raises practical questions on responsibility, access and how staff feel about working alongside it.

top_stories.title: Claude adds live dashboards and animation
top_stories.what: Anthropic released Claude Dashboards, which turn plain questions into live charts from company data, and Claude Motion, which builds editable animations from reports.
top_stories.why: Analysts without coding skills can now build and refresh data views quickly, so data governance matters more than ever.

saudi_lens.text: As Saudi entities adopt AI agents with their own accounts and permissions, national data and cybersecurity rules will need clear guidance on agent identities and audit trails.

idea.title: Working with AI coworkers study
idea.pitch: Interview and survey staff in organisations piloting AI agents on trust, workload and who they think is responsible when things go wrong.
idea.first_step: Draft an interview guide with eight questions on trust, control and accountability.

idea_kids.title: Check my answer game
idea_kids.pitch: Pairs of children solve simple puzzles, then swap and check each other's work step by step before any answer is accepted.
idea_kids.first_step: Print ten short puzzles with space for a checker's tick at each step.

terms.definition: When independent experts check research before it is accepted as reliable.
Using a computer to check, step by step, that a proof or program is correct.
A record of who or what did each action in a system, so mistakes can be traced.

concepts.summary: AI produces research faster than peer review can check it.
Agents that keep working for days with their own accounts and memory.
AI suites that turn questions into documents, dashboards and animations.
